text:
What mass of LiCl (molar mass 42.4 g/mol) contains the same number of
moles of Cl- ions as 242 g of RbCl (molar mass 121 g/mol)?
explanation: 242 g of RbCl corresponds to 242/121 = 2.00 mol RbCl, which provides 2.00 mol Cl⁻. LiCl also provides 1 mol Cl⁻ per mole of LiCl, so 2.00 mol LiCl is needed. Its mass is 2.00 mol × 42.4 g/mol = 84.8 g.

as Ca2+?

options.C: Mg2+
options.D: Sr2+

text:
When 28 g of Fe(s) reacts with 32 g of O2(g), what is the maximum mass of
Fe2O3(s) (molar mass 160. g/mol) that can be produced?
Iron metal reacts with oxygen gas to produce iron(III) oxide, as represented by
the equation given.

4 Fe(s)+3 O2(g)→2 Fe2O3(s)
explanation: 28 g Fe is 0.50 mol Fe and 32 g O2 is 1.0 mol O2. The reaction requires 4 mol Fe per 3 mol O2, so Fe is the limiting reactant. Produced Fe2O3 = 0.50 mol Fe × (2 mol Fe2O3 / 4 mol Fe) = 0.25 mol, which is 0.25 × 160 g/mol = 40 g.

Which of the following correctly predicts the position of the piston at the
completion of the reaction?
A mixture of 0.02 mol of H2(g) and 0.01 mol of O2(g) is pumped into a
cylinder with a movable piston, as shown.

The mixture, originally at 200°C and 1.0 atm, is sparked and the gases react
until the reactants are completely consumed according to the equation
provided.
2 H2(g)+O2(g)→2 H2O(g)
At the completion of the reaction, the contents of the cylinder are cooled to
the original temperature, 200°C.

options.A:
The piston will be higher because the number of gas molecules in the
products is greater than that in the reactants.
options.B:
The piston will be at its original position because the total mass of the gases
in the cylinder does not change.
options.C:
The piston will be at its original position because the gases in the cylinder will
be at the original temperature and pressure.
options.D:
The piston will be lower because the number of gas molecules in the products
is less than that in the reactants.

explanation: The reaction consumes 0.02 mol H2 and 0.01 mol O2 to produce 0.02 mol H2O(g). Initially there are 0.03 mol gas; finally there are 0.02 mol gas. At constant temperature and pressure, volume is proportional to moles of gas, so the volume decreases and the piston moves lower.

text:
The melting point of KBr is 734°C, and the melting point of RbBr is 682°C.
Based on Coulomb’s law, which of the following best explains the difference in
melting points?

options.A: The ionic radius of K+ is larger than that of Br-.
options.B: The ionic radius of Rb+ is larger than that of Br-.
options.C: The ionic radius of K+ is larger than that of Rb+.
options.D: The ionic radius of Rb+ is larger than that of K+.

explanation: Rb+ has a larger ionic radius than K+. Since both salts have +1/-1 charges, the difference in melting point is due to ion separation. RbBr has a greater distance between its ions, so the Coulombic attraction is weaker, giving a lower melting point.

of the ion and the hybridization of the nitrogen atom?

options.A: Linear, sp
options.B: Linear, sp2
options.C: Bent, sp2
options.D: Bent, sp3

explanation: In NO2-, nitrogen has two bonding domains (one single bond to O- and one double bond to O) and one lone pair, giving a steric number of 3. This corresponds to sp2 hybridization and a bent molecular geometry.

relationship between the atomic radii and the structures of these atoms?

options.A:
140 pm; as the number of protons decreases for elements in the same period,
the atomic radius increases.
options.B:
140 pm; as the mass of the nucleus decreases for elements in the same period,
the atomic radius increases.
options.C:
100 pm; as the number of electrons decreases for elements in the same period,
the atomic radius decreases.
options.D:
100 pm; as the mass of the nucleus increases for elements in the same period,
the atomic radius decreases.

explanation: Magnesium is to the left of aluminum in the same period, so it has fewer protons and a larger atomic radius. Thus, Mg is about 140 pm, and the trend is that atomic radius increases as the number of protons decreases across a period.

text: Which of the following bonds is the most polar?

valid justification?

shown.
2 K2O2(s)+2 H2O(l)→4 KOH(aq)+O2(g)

options.A:
A redox reaction, because the oxidation number of O changes from -1 to -2
and from -1 to 0.
options.B:
A redox reaction, because the oxidation number of K changes from +2 to +1
and that of H changes from +1 to -1.
options.C: An acid-base reaction, because H+ is transferred between oxygen atoms.

explanation: This is a redox reaction because oxygen in the peroxide ion has an oxidation number of -1 and is both reduced to -2 in KOH and oxidized to 0 in O2 gas.

text:
Which of the following indicates the side of the equilibrium that is favored
and helps explain why?
Consider the following reaction.

C2H5COO-(aq)+HCO3-(aq)⇄C2H5COOH(aq)+CO32-(aq)
The value of Ka for HCO3-(aq) is 4.8×10-11, and the value of Ka for
C2H5COOH(aq) is 1.3×10-5.

options.A:
The products are favored because C2H5COO-(aq) has a greater affinity for
H+(aq) than CO32-(aq) does.
options.B:
The products are favored because CO32-(aq) has a greater affinity for H+(aq)
than C2H5COO-(aq) does.
options.C:
The reactants are favored because C2H5COO-(aq) has a greater affinity for
H+(aq) than CO32-(aq) does.
options.D:
The reactants are favored because CO32-(aq) has a greater affinity for H+(aq)
than C2H5COO-(aq) does.

explanation: The equilibrium favors the side with the weaker acid and weaker base. Here, HCO3- (Ka = 4.8×10^-11) is a much weaker acid than C2H5COOH (Ka = 1.3×10^-5), so the reverse reaction is favored, meaning reactants are favored. Also, CO3^2- is a stronger base (greater affinity for H+) than C2H5COO-, so it will tend to accept a proton and reform reactants.

temperature. Which of the following correctly compares the solubility of the
Ag2CrO4(s) salt in a 0.050 M solution of AgNO3(aq) to the salt’s solubility in
water at the same temperature?

options.A:
The solubility is greater in AgNO3(aq) because AgNO3(s) has a lower molar
mass than Ag2CrO4(s) does.
options.B:
The solubility is less in AgNO3(aq) because the solution already contains
Ag+(aq).
options.C: The solubility is the same because it is equal to [CrO42-].
options.D:
The solubility is the same because the Ksp changes only with a change in

explanation: AgNO3 provides Ag+ ions, which is a common ion to the dissociation of Ag2CrO4. The common ion effect shifts the dissolution equilibrium toward the solid, decreasing the solubility of Ag2CrO4 compared to pure water.

and provides the best explanation based on VSEPR theory?
A Lewis diagram of OF2 is shown.

options.A:
The bond angle is 103° because the lone pairs of electrons on the O atom
repel more strongly than the bonding pairs do.
options.B: The bond angle is 103° because the F atoms have four electron domains.

text:
What is the initial concentration of the LiOH(aq)?
A student titrates a 20.0 mL sample of LiOH(aq) using the setup shown. The
student uses a 0.80 M solution of HCl to titrate the base. The initial buret
reading for the HCl is 9.0 mL. The buret reading at the equivalence point is
shown in the magnified view of the buret.

The numbers on the magnified view of the buret range from 11 to 13,
top to bottom.

Between each integer value on the buret are 4 tick marks.

A concave meniscus at the top of the solution is drawn as follows:

o

The highest points of the meniscus touch the 1st tick mark below
11.
o
o
The lowest point of the meniscus touches the 2nd tick mark
below 11.
o
explanation: The buret is read at the bottom of the concave meniscus, which is at the 2nd tick mark below 11. With 4 tick marks between integer mL values, each tick is 0.2 mL, so the final buret reading is 11.4 mL. HCl delivered = 11.4 mL - 9.0 mL = 2.4 mL = 0.0024 L. Moles HCl = 0.80 M × 0.0024 L = 0.00192 mol. At equivalence, moles LiOH = moles HCl = 0.00192 mol, so [LiOH] = 0.00192 mol / 0.0200 L = 0.096 M.

explanation: The initial state shows two separate gases in a divided container, each occupying half the volume. When the divider is removed, the gases mix and expand to fill the entire container. Which of the following is the best Lewis diagram for the N2O molecule based
on formal charges?

options.A: See option A in the attached figure
options.B: See option B in the attached figure
options.C: See option C in the attached figure
options.D: See option D in the attached figure

explanation: The best Lewis structure for N2O is determined by minimizing formal charges and placing negative formal charges on the more electronegative atoms. In option D, the structure is N≡N–O with lone pairs arranged such that the left nitrogen has a formal charge of 0, the central nitrogen has a formal charge of +1, and the oxygen has a formal charge of -1. This is favorable because the more electronegative oxygen carries the negative charge. The formal charges are: N (left) = 5 - (2 + 3) = 0, N (central) = 5 - (0 + 4) = +1, O = 6 - (6 + 1) = -1. The sum is 0, and the negative charge is on oxygen, which is more electronegative than nitrogen. This makes D the best structure based on formal charges. The other options either have higher formal charges or place negative charges on less electronegative atoms, making them less stable.

options.C: ns2 np4
options.D: ns2 np5

explanation: The large jump between the fourth and fifth ionization energies indicates that the fifth electron is removed from a stable core, so the element has 4 valence electrons. Therefore, the valence configuration is ns2 np2.

text:
Which of the following gives the correct rate law for the elementary step
represented by the equation provided?
2 NO(g)+O2(g)→2 NO2(g)

options.A: rate=kNO2O2
options.B: rate=kNO2O2[NO2]2
options.C: rate=kNO22NO2O2
options.D: rate=k[NO]2O2NO22

explanation: For an elementary step, the rate law is determined directly from the balanced reaction: each reactant's concentration is raised to its stoichiometric coefficient. Thus rate = k[NO]^2[O2], which corresponds to choice A.

text:
A current of 0.20 C/s is passed through 150 mL of a 1.0 M solution of copper(II)
nitrate, CuNO32, for 4850 seconds, forming copper metal. How many moles of
copper metal are deposited during this time?
explanation: Charge passed = 0.20 C/s × 4850 s = 970 C. Moles of electrons = 970 C / 96485 C/mol ≈ 0.01005 mol e⁻. For Cu²⁺ deposition, Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu, so moles Cu = 0.01005 / 2 ≈ 5.0×10⁻³ mol.

text:
The particle diagram most likely represents an aqueous solution of which of
the following acids? (Water molecules are not shown.)
A particle diagram is shown.

options.A: HBrO
options.B: HNO2
options.C: HClO4
options.D: HC2 H3O2

explanation: The particle diagram shows a solution with both ions and neutral molecules, indicating partial dissociation. HNO2 (nitrous acid) is a weak acid that only partially dissociates in water, producing H+ and NO2- ions along with undissociated HNO2 molecules. This matches the diagram. HBrO and HC2H3O2 are also weak acids, but HClO4 is a strong acid that fully dissociates, which would show only ions, not molecules. Thus, the diagram most likely represents HNO2.

text:
Which of the following graphs is most likely the energy profile of the chemical
reaction?
An exothermic chemical reaction involves a two-step reaction mechanism. The
rate law of the reaction is the same as the rate law for the first elementary step.

options.A:
As reaction progress increases, the energy increases to a relative
maximum twice.

The first maximum is much higher than the second maximum.

There is a relative minimum between the two maximums.

The amount of energy at the relative minimum is higher than the
amount of energy at the start of the reaction.

The amount of energy at the end of the reaction is lower than the
amount of energy at the start of the reaction.
options.B:
As reaction progress increases, the energy increases to a relative
maximum twice.

The first maximum is much lower than the second maximum.

There is a relative minimum between the two maximums.

The amount of energy at the relative minimum is higher than the
amount of energy at the start of the reaction.

The amount of energy at the end of the reaction is much lower than the
amount of energy at the start of the reaction.
options.C:
As reaction progress increases, the energy increases to a relative
maximum twice.

The first maximum is much lower than the second maximum.

There is an absolute minimum between the two relative maximums.

The amount of energy at the absolute minimum is lower than the
amount of energy at the start of the reaction.

The amount of energy at the end of the reaction is higher than the
amount of energy at the start of the reaction.
options.D:
As reaction progress increases, the energy increases to a relative
maximum twice.

The first maximum is slightly higher than the second maximum.

There is a relative minimum between the two maximums.

The amount of energy at the relative minimum is higher than the
amount of energy at the start of the reaction.

The amount of energy at the end of the reaction is slightly higher than
the amount of energy at the start of the reaction.

explanation: The reaction is exothermic, so the products must lie below the reactants. Because the first elementary step determines the rate law, the first step is rate-determining and has the larger activation barrier; therefore the first peak is higher than the second, which is shown in choice A.
